cards.name: J-cut and L-cut (split edits)
cards.summary: A split edit: the sound of the next shot starts before its picture (J-cut) or the sound of the outgoing shot carries on under the next picture (L-cut). The everyday grammar of interviews and documentaries: the cut feels smooth because sound and picture do not change on the same frame.
use_for: interview and documentary cutting (J-cut into a speaker, L-cut out onto b-roll)
softening a hard cut
letting a reaction shot play under the speaker's line
cards.how: Premiere: turn off Linked Selection (the timeline toggle) or hold Alt and click to select only the audio or only the video of a clip, then drag that edit point (or use the Rolling Edit tool, N, on the audio edit only); Clip > Unlink splits a clip for good (Ctrl+L links again). Working default: audio leads or trails by 0.3-1.5 s, with a short audio crossfade on the overlap. After Effects has no linked audio: offset the audio layer's in point. Bridge: a clip's own audio travels with it, so build a split edit with a separate audio[] entry cut from the same file (src = the video file, its own start / in / dur) on another track.
cards.script_api: ExtendScript: select the pair (TrackItem.setSelected(true, true)), Sequence.unlinkSelection(), then trim the audio TrackItem alone (its end / start); Sequence.linkSelection() re-links. Or place picture and sound separately with Sequence.insertClip / overwriteClip(projectItem, time, vTrackIndex, aTrackIndex).
cards.limits: Whether writing TrackItem.start moves or trims an item was not verified (PVE TrackItem card), so scripted J/L cuts should change the outgoing audio's end (L) or place the incoming audio earlier as its own clip (J). In an L-cut both shots' audio overlaps: lower or cut the incoming clip's own audio for that stretch.

cards.name: Trims: ripple, roll, slip and slide
cards.summary: The four trims: Ripple Edit (B) changes one clip's length and moves everything after it; Rolling Edit (N) moves the cut between two clips without changing the sequence length; Slip (Y) changes which part of a clip is used without moving it; Slide (U) moves a clip along the track and trims its neighbours to keep the length.
use_for: tightening an interview without leaving gaps (ripple)
moving a cut to a better frame (roll)
choosing a better moment of a b-roll shot in place (slip)
re-timing a shot against the music (slide)
cards.how: Tools: Ripple Edit B, Rolling Edit N, Slip Y, Slide U (Adobe's trim pages). Scripted equivalents with the official DOM (it has no trim tools): ripple = set an item's end, then move every later item on the track(s) by the same delta (TrackItem.move); roll = A's end and B's head together by the same delta; slip = shift inPoint and outPoint by the same delta and keep start / end; slide = move the item and adjust the neighbours' end / start. QE has slip / slide / roll methods, all unsupported and unverified.
cards.script_api: TrackItem.start, end, inPoint, outPoint (Time, read/write), TrackItem.move(Time), TrackItem.remove(inRipple, inAlignToVideo); QE: QETrackItem.slip(...), slide(...), roll(...) (unverified signatures)
cards.limits: How writing start / inPoint behaves (move vs trim) is unverified on 26.0.2: read every item back after a scripted trim. Linked audio follows only UI trims on a linked pair; scripts should trim audio and video items explicitly. A slip or roll needs media beyond the in / out points (handles).

cards.name: Three-point and four-point edits (insert and overwrite)
cards.summary: Placing a shot by marks: set three of source In, source Out, sequence In and sequence Out and the fourth follows; Insert (,) pushes later clips along, Overwrite (.) replaces what is there. With all four set, Premiere asks how to fit the clip (one choice changes its speed: fit to fill).
use_for: cutting a sound bite into the timeline at an exact point
laying b-roll over a range without moving the edit
fit-to-fill a shot into a gap
cards.how: Source Monitor: mark In (I) and Out (O); in the timeline set the target (playhead or sequence In); patch the source tracks; press , (Insert) or . (Overwrite). With an Insert edit, Adobe notes, the later clips shift ahead to make room. Four-point: set both pairs, then pick a Fit Clip option.
cards.script_api: ProjectItem.setInPoint(seconds, 4) / setOutPoint(seconds, 4) (4 = all media types, as pr_build.jsx uses), then Sequence.insertClip(projectItem, time, vTrackIndex, aTrackIndex) or Sequence.overwriteClip(projectItem, time, vTrackIndex, aTrackIndex); UXP: SequenceEditor insert / overwrite actions.
cards.limits: The Fit Clip dialog's option names ('Change Clip Speed (Fit to Fill)', 'Ignore Source In/Out Point' ...) were found only in third-party guides, not on Adobe's pages. The docs type insertClip's time as Time but overwriteClip's as a seconds string: pass what the installed build accepts (pr_build.jsx passes seconds to overwriteClip). In / Out set on a ProjectItem affect every later use of that item.

cards.name: Replace edit (Replace With Clip)
cards.summary: Swapping the media of a shot already in the timeline while keeping its position, length and effects: the replace edit, used to try alternative takes or b-roll without rebuilding effects and keyframes.
use_for: trying alternative takes of a shot
swapping placeholder footage for the final
versioning a template edit
cards.how: Premiere UI: right-click the timeline clip > Replace With Clip > From Source Monitor (or From Bin), or Alt-drag a clip from the Project panel onto the timeline clip (community-documented; no current Adobe help page and no default shortcut row were found). To replace a file everywhere it is used: relink it ('Relink offline media').
cards.script_api: No replace-edit call in the ExtendScript DOM; equivalents: ProjectItem.changeMediaPath(newPath) (every use of the item), or overwriteClip at the same start and re-apply the effects (they do not carry over).
cards.limits: Menu names come from community sources and older docs, not a current Adobe page: low confidence until checked in the installed build.

cards.name: Lift and Extract (remove a range)
cards.summary: Removing a marked range from the sequence: Lift (;) leaves a gap, Extract (') closes it by pulling the later clips back (a ripple delete of the range).
use_for: cutting a sentence out of an interview (extract)
blanking a range to fill with b-roll later (lift)
cards.how: Set sequence In and Out around the range, target the tracks, press ; (Lift) or ' (Extract). Whole clips: select them and Ripple Delete (Shift+Delete).
cards.script_api: Whole clips: TrackItem.remove(false, true) = lift, TrackItem.remove(true, true) = ripple delete (with inRipple set, later track items move earlier to fill the gap). A range inside clips needs a cut at both ends first (QE razor, unsupported) or trimming the overlapping items' end / start, then moving later items back by the range length.
cards.limits: No range-based Lift / Extract call in the DOM. remove()'s description on the docs page is copied from setSelected (a doc error): its parameter table is the reliable part.

cards.name: Match frame and reverse match frame
cards.summary: Match Frame (F) opens the timeline shot's source clip at the same frame in the Source Monitor; Reverse Match Frame (Shift+R) finds where the Source Monitor's frame is used in the sequence.
use_for: finding the rest of a shot to extend or replace it
checking where a source moment was used
re-cutting from the original after a nest or render
cards.how: Park on the shot (target its track) and press F; in the Source Monitor press Shift+R to jump to its use in the sequence. Scripted: source time = trackItem.inPoint.seconds + (t - trackItem.start.seconds) for a clip at 100% speed; reverse = search the track items whose projectItem.nodeId matches and whose inPoint..outPoint holds the time.
cards.script_api: TrackItem.start / inPoint / projectItem / getSpeed(); ProjectItem.nodeId; Sequence.setPlayerPosition (PVE Sequence housekeeping card)
cards.limits: Speed-changed or time-remapped clips break the simple formula (getSpeed() gives a constant speed only). Nested sequences match to the nest, not to its contents.

cards.name: Closing gaps (Ripple Delete, Close Gap)
cards.summary: Removing empty space left by deletes and lifts: Ripple Delete on a gap or a clip closes it; Sequence > Close Gap closes every gap on the targeted tracks.
use_for: tidying a rough cut
after scripted removals that left holes
before export, to catch accidental black frames
cards.how: Select a gap and press Delete, or a clip and Shift+Delete (Ripple Delete; Alt+Backspace is the timeline-panel entry); Sequence > Close Gap for all gaps (reported by community sources; no Adobe help page found). Scripted: per track, sort items by start and move each one earlier by the gap before it (TrackItem.move), moving linked audio and video items together.
cards.script_api: TrackItem.move(Time) (15.4+ per PVE's TrackItem card), TrackItem.start / end; Track.clips
cards.limits: Closing gaps on one track only desyncs linked clips on the others: close them across every track of a linked pair. The Close Gap menu item is not confirmed on Adobe's pages.

cards.name: Edit grammar on After Effects layers (trim, slip, ripple by script)
cards.summary: After Effects has no edit tools beyond layer trims, so edit grammar is three numbers per layer: startTime (where the source's first frame sits), inPoint and outPoint. Slip = move startTime only; ripple = shift the later layers; split audio = a separate audio layer with its own in point.
use_for: mirroring a Premiere edit in AE (the bridge does)
slipping a shot inside a precomp
scripted ripple trims
cards.how: Trim: layer.inPoint / outPoint (Alt+[ and Alt+] in the UI). Slip: layer.startTime -= d with in / out unchanged (the visible range moves through the source). Ripple: after changing one layer's outPoint by d, add d to the startTime of every layer that begins after it. ae_build.jsx places clips exactly this way (startTime = start - in, inPoint = start, outPoint = start + dur).
cards.limits: Set startTime before inPoint / outPoint, or the in / out can clamp against the source's extent. Time-stretched layers (stretch other than 100) scale source time.
